complete_source_mathematical_review.reason: The source is quoted faithfully modulo typesetting, bilingual agreement is correctly stated, and the report explicitly chooses the established edge-ring interpretation already approved in source preassessment. The counterexample refutes the necessity direction of the exact cutoff and satisfies n>0.

The edge set includes every unordered pair of distinct vertices. The map is coefficient-preserving and sends each edge variable to the product of its endpoints. The kernel is the stated toric ideal. Multisets are arbitrary natural exponent vectors and degree equality is at each labeled vertex.

Occurrence removals correctly account for multiplicities. In the common-neighbor case the equations 2+s_c=q_c and |Q|=|S|+1 imply s_c<|S|; this forces an avoiding edge in the residual multiset. Orientation x different from a suffices for all newly created edges. Both replacements preserve endpoint counts, and reflexive cases are explicitly harmless. This matches insert_edge.

Induction on target edge count with arbitrary source inserts one edge, cancels its endpoint multiset, applies the smaller-target induction, and lifts by a common edge. The proof covers all degrees and all multiplicities, matching connected_of_degree_eq.

complete_source_mathematical_review.claim: Finite nonzero quadrics and binomial membership
complete_source_mathematical_review.reason: The common set of all distinct equal-degree two-edge differences is finite for finite E. Distinct monomials with coefficient one yield nonzero homogeneous quadrics over every nontrivial commutative ring. Common contexts multiply generators and finite paths telescope, exactly matching the Lean ideal-membership induction.

The quotient argument groups arbitrary finite polynomial coefficients by image exponent, uses equal-fiber binomial membership to identify quotient classes, and obtains zero quotient class from coefficientwise vanishing. This remains valid with zero divisors and matches the generic IdealBridge proof. The reverse inclusion is also included, giving actual ideal equality.

The report establishes the stronger arbitrary-finite-complete-graph result over nontrivial commutative rings, specializes to all fields and K6, and identifies the actual positive-domain Lean negation. It uses the corrected CompleteGraph.connected_of_degree_eq name. The displayed eval2Hom identity uses a typeset subscript 2 corresponding to the Lean Unicode subscript.

The report gives both finite binomial generation and all-fiber connectivity. Redundancy and both signs are permitted under the standard generating-set definition. If inclusion-minimal terminology is preferred, taking a minimal subset of this finite generating set preserves degree two; no new source assumption is needed.
